headline: Sensex tumbles 548 points as oil price spike and FII outflows drag Indian markets below key levels

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Oil price spikes triggered concerns across global and domestic equity markets.
Persistent Foreign Institutional Investor (FII) outflows weighed down market sentiment.
Drag in major sectors including IT, FMCG, and financial stocks pulled indices lower.
Impact from recent RBI policy measures affected domestic fixed income and broader markets.
whatHappening: Sensex dropped 548 points while Nifty 50 slipped below the key 22,400 level.
HCL Tech declared a Rs 12 interim dividend for FY27 as Q2 profit surged 21% YoY to Rs 5,132 crore.
PVR Inox touched its 52-week high after rallying up to 13% over the past month.
Sahajanand Medical Technologies announced its IPO price band of Rs 327-344 per share opening Oct 15.
summary: Indian markets fell sharply on October 12, with Sensex dropping 548 points and Nifty sliding below 22,400 amid surging oil prices and heavy FII selling. Broad drag in IT, FMCG, and financial sectors compounded the market decline. Despite the downturn, HCL Tech reported a 21% jump in Q2 profit and PVR Inox hit a 52-week high.
